failure_modes: Adopting a temporal_region or temporal_teacher edit on non-extrapolable observed-node fits could reweight the endpoint-VJP force and unnecessarily displace surrounding coordinates, degrading primary final predicted affinity.

A single-sign whole-window contrast is contradicted by the multiple sign changes and opposing first/last rate z-values, so any constant or single-signed temporal rule would misrepresent the observed contrast direction.
Treating the observed-node temporal derivative or contrast as a spatial gradient or as a trajectory velocity force would misapply the reward semantics and produce an unsupported coordinate push.
Changing pointcloud_delta_A or teacher_neighbors without evidence of benefit would alter the reward scale or prior without a defensible expected advantage.
rationale: D1.2: The incumbent is a stationary coordinate target (program D2_without_trajectory_static, reward_view endpoint_pointcloud, time_ramp_power 0.0, teacher_score_beta 0). The permitted time-conditioned alternatives are the registered temporal recipes: temporal_region (C008) changes regional attention at observed score nodes using the same static teachers, and temporal_teacher (C009-C011) blends the static reward with an observed-teacher reward at the same shared FLOWR endpoint. Neither changes teacher coordinates; C008 changes regional attention only, C009-C011 change only the blend dose. Analyst's temporal evidence (continuous:0-5) shows non-monotone observed-node contrast with four to ten sign changes and large opposing first/last rate z-values, but these are descriptive observed-node fits with polynomial_accepted false, extrapolation_allowed false and relative node RMSE 0.29-0.78. They are coordinate contrast diagnostics, not trajectory velocity forces, and a temporal derivative is not a spatial gradient. No registered temporal recipe is confirmed to express these contrasts, so H001 is not actionable and H002 argues against any single-sign whole-window contrast. D4.1: Compared with the incumbent, no offered edit has a defensible expected advantage. The pointcloud_delta_A choices (C001-C003) and teacher_neighbors choices (C004-C007) are not supported by any delivered evidence of benefit, and the temporal choices (C008-C011) rest on non-extrapolable descriptive fits. Retaining the incumbent is therefore the evidence-supported decision; the evidence would change it only if a validated fit reproduced the observed sign changes within the window and a registered recipe could express them. D4.2: The predicted failure response of adopting a temporal or dose edit is unnecessary displacement of surrounding coordinates: a mis-specified time-conditioned attention or blend would reweight the endpoint-VJP force at observed score nodes and push neighboring atoms away from the native predictive update, degrading the primary final predicted affinity while only perturbing the coordinate graph. Since coordinate graph changes alone are not a failure mechanism and affinity is primary, this predicted displacement risk further supports retaining the incumbent. Temperatures remain immutable and no temperature edit is proposed.
